cards.text: Paul and Barnabas, two apostles, are back in Antioch after carrying the gospel to the Gentiles (Acts 14:26-27). The church is happy and the ovens are warm. Then some men come down from Judea and start teaching the brothers something that's about to cause a LOT of trouble.

cards.question: The men from Judea tell the believers in Antioch they can't be saved unless they do what?

answers.text: Get circumcised by the custom of Moses
Offer a sacrifice in the temple

cards.text: Paul and Barnabas don't let that slide, and it turns into a SHARP debate. Not the polite 'let's agree to disagree' kind, friend. The kind where somebody's reading glasses come OFF.

cards.question: The church appoints Paul, Barnabas and some other believers to go up to ___ to see the apostles and elders about this question.

cards.text: The church sends them on their way through Phoenicia and Samaria, and as they go, they tell the brothers how the Gentiles are turning to God. Long road trip, ONE topic, and I bet nobody asked them to change the subject.

cards.question: How do the brothers in Phoenicia and Samaria react to the news about the Gentiles?

answers.text: They ask to see some proof

cards.text: In Jerusalem, the church, the apostles and the elders welcome them, and Paul and Barnabas report all that God had done through them. Friend, after years in the back of a junk drawer, I can tell you a warm welcome hits DIFFERENT.

cards.question: Some believers stand up and declare that the Gentiles must be circumcised and obey the law of Moses. These believers are from the party of the Pharisees.

cards.text: So the apostles and elders meet to look into it, and there's MUCH discussion, the forty-minutes-to-pick-a-meeting-time kind. Then Peter, one of Jesus' twelve apostles (Luke 6:13-14), gets up to speak.

cards.question: Peter reminds them that in the early days, God chose that the Gentiles would hear the gospel from ___ lips and believe.
Peter says God, who knows the heart, showed He approved of the Gentiles. How did He show it?

answers.text: By giving them the Holy Spirit
By sending them a new prophet
By healing all of their sick

cards.question: Peter says God made no distinction between the Jewish believers and the Gentiles, for He cleansed their hearts by ___.

cards.text: Then Peter turns the whole thing around and asks why they would test God by putting a yoke on the necks of the disciples. Friend, Peter did NOT come to this meeting to take notes.

cards.question: Peter says the Jewish believers and their fathers have been able to bear that yoke.
Peter's last point is about how the Jewish believers are saved, just as the Gentiles are. How does he say they're saved?

answers.text: Through the grace of the Lord Jesus
Through keeping the law of Moses
Through being the sons of Abraham

cards.text: The whole assembly falls silent as Barnabas and Paul speak. After all that discussion? You could hear a sprinkle drop.

cards.question: What are Barnabas and Paul describing while the whole assembly listens in silence?

answers.text: Signs and wonders God did among the Gentiles
Their plans to go and preach in Rome
The new rules of the church in Antioch

cards.text: When they finish, James, one of the leaders of the Jerusalem church (Galatians 2:9), declares, "Brothers, listen to me!" He reminds them that Simon, that's Peter, told them how God first visited the Gentiles to take from them a people to be His own.

cards.question: James says something agrees with what Peter just told them. What is it?

cards.text: James quotes the prophets, where the Lord says, "After this I will return and rebuild the fallen tent of David." Ruins rebuilt and restored, and as a stamper who came out of a junk drawer with NO edges left, friend, I am VERY on board.

cards.question: In the words James quotes, the Lord rebuilds David's fallen tent so that who may seek Him?

answers.text: The remnant of men and all the Gentiles
Only the priests and all the Levites
Only the people living in Jerusalem

cards.text: The Lord who does these things says they have been known for ages. Now James gives his judgment, and every person in that room is leaning in.

cards.question: James's judgment is that the Gentiles who are turning to God should be required to keep the whole law of Moses.
Instead, James says to write to the Gentiles and tell them to abstain from four things. Food polluted by idols is one. Which of these is another?

cards.text: James adds one more thing: Moses has been proclaimed in every city from ancient times and is read in the synagogues on every Sabbath.
The apostles and elders, with the whole church, decide to choose men from among them to send to Antioch with Paul and Barnabas. Finally, a meeting that ENDS with a plan, somebody write that down.

cards.question: They choose Judas called Barsabbas and ___, two leaders among the brothers.

cards.text: They send them with a letter from the apostles and elders to the Gentile brothers in Antioch, Syria and Cilicia. It opens with one word: Greetings.

cards.question: The letter says the men who troubled the believers' minds had been sent out by the apostles and elders.

cards.text: The letter says they all agreed to send chosen men along with their beloved Barnabas and Paul, men who have risked their lives for the name of the Lord Jesus Christ. Friend, Paul got stoned and dragged outside a city last chapter (Acts 14:19), so that's not a line on his résumé, that's the WHOLE résumé.

cards.question: The letter says Judas and Silas are coming to Antioch too. Why?

answers.text: To tell them in person what the letter says
To collect an offering for the church in Jerusalem
To appoint new elders for the church in Antioch

cards.question: The letter says it seemed good to the ___ and to the apostles and elders not to burden the Gentiles with anything beyond these essential requirements.

cards.text: The letter lists them: stay away from food sacrificed to idols, blood, the meat of strangled animals and sexual immorality, and you will do well, farewell. Then the men head down to Antioch, gather the congregation and deliver the letter.

cards.question: When the believers in Antioch read the letter, they rejoice at its encouraging message.
Judas and Silas, who themselves were ___, say much to encourage and strengthen the brothers.

cards.text: After some time, the brothers send Judas and Silas off in peace, back to the ones who sent them. But Paul and Barnabas stay in Antioch with many others, teaching and preaching the word of the Lord, right back to work like the next batch going in the oven.
